preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 10**5 for n in [int(input().split()[0]) for _ in range(t)])
preconditions.description: Each test case has an integer n between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(s) == 2 * n for n, s in [(int(input().split()[0]), input().strip()) for _ in range(t)])
preconditions.description: Each binary string s has length 2n.

preconditions.expression: all(all(c in '01' for c in s) for n, s in [(int(input().split()[0]), input().strip()) for _ in range(t)])
preconditions.description: Each binary string s consists only of characters '0' and '1'.

preconditions.expression: sum(n for n, s in [(int(input().split()[0]), input().strip()) for _ in range(t)]) <= 10**5
preconditions.description: The sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 100,000.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or (len(return_value.split()) == 2 * n + 1 and all(int(x) >= 1 and int(x) <= 2 * n for x in return_value.split()[1:]))
postconditions.description: The output is either '-1' or consists of 2n+1 integers where the first integer m is between 0 and 2n inclusive, and the next m integers are distinct indices between 1 and 2n inclusive, followed by n distinct indices between 1 and 2n inclusive.
If the output is not '-1', the first m integers are distinct.
If the output is not '-1', the last n integers are distinct.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or all(int(x) >= 1 and int(x) <= 2 * n for x in return_value.split()[1 + int(return_value.split()[0]):])
postconditions.description: If the output is not '-1', the last n integers are between 1 and 2n inclusive.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or (lambda s, b, p: ''.join(s[i-1] for i in p) == ''.join(s[i-1] for i in p) and all(s[i-1] == s[j-1] for i, j in zip(p, p[1:] + p[:1])))((lambda n, s: (n, s))(*map(int, input().split())), list(map(int, return_value.split()[1:1 + int(return_value.split()[0])])), list(map(int, return_value.split()[1 + int(return_value.split()[0]):]))
postconditions.description: If the output is not '-1', the string formed by the indices in p is equal to the string formed by the indices in p after rotating the subsequence b.
